capital.heading: Recovery funding, and every child a reader.

EIB Group financing in Slovakia in 2025, up 60% on 2024, led by energy-network upgrades and urban development (reported 27 March 2026)
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Ten-year euro government bond
register.detail: ARDAL, the Debt and Liquidity Management Agency · sold 23 September 2026 · new ten-year state bonds
register.note: A budget-wide bond; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: New ten-year government bonds of the Slovak Republic, sold on the financial market by ARDAL. They fund the state budget as a whole; their proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Three-, six- and ten-year bonds in Swiss francs
register.detail: ARDAL · sold 6 May 2026 · maturities of three, six and ten years · the previous issue in Swiss francs, of CHF 635M, was sold in April 2024
register.note: A budget-wide bond; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: New government bonds of the Slovak Republic in Swiss francs, sold by ARDAL in three maturities. They fund the state budget as a whole; their proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Loans for the social economy and social housing, SIH and Slovenská sporiteľňa
register.detail: Slovak Investment Holding · announced 4 May 2026 · each loan financed 50:50 by SIH and Slovenská sporiteľňa · the SIH share is interest-free
register.note: For social economy entities, projects with a significant social impact and affordable housing for disadvantaged groups; no volume stated
register.text: A loan instrument under which Slovak Investment Holding (SIH) and Slovenská sporiteľňa finance each loan half and half, with the SIH share interest-free, so the rate for the borrower is significantly reduced. It lends to social economy entities and to affordable housing for disadvantaged groups, serving the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Twenty-year euro government bond
register.detail: ARDAL · sold 11 February 2026 · new twenty-year state bonds
register.note: A budget-wide bond; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: New twenty-year government bonds of the Slovak Republic, sold on the financial market by ARDAL. They fund the state budget as a whole; their proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Regional investment programme, Banská Bystrica Self-Governing Region
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 10 December 2025 · announced 9 November 2026 · with an EU grant of €5M under the Just Transition Mechanism · programme worth around €36.5M
register.note: Around 100 projects, including schools in Banská Bystrica and Zvolen and social care facilities in Krupina
register.text: An EIB loan, with an accompanying EU grant, to Slovakia’s largest region by area for around 100 projects. It upgrades schools in Banská Bystrica and Zvolen and social care facilities in Krupina, serving the education standard, the standard furthest from reach in Slovakia.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · €6.408bn, entirely in grants, including a REPowerEU grant of €366.4M · €822.7M pre-financing · seven instalments authorised, the sixth and seventh on 24 April 2026 · eighth payment request, for €548M, partially assessed positively
register.note: Final payment requests were due by 30 September 2026; all payments must be completed by 31 December 2026
register.text: EU Recovery and Resilience Facility funding for Slovakia’s reforms and investments, entirely in grants. It finances the modernisation of hospital buildings (€1.1 billion), the energy renovation of family houses (€446.5 million), digital equipment for schools (€187 million) and more pre-school places (€141 million), serving the health, shelter, energy and education standards.

register.name: Sustainable urban development, City of Košice
register.detail: European Investment Bank · up to €20M · announced 25 June 2026 · with an EU grant of €4.3M from the Public Sector Loan Facility · around 85% of the investment for climate action
register.note: Modernised primary schools, a centre for mothers with children, a new senior care facility and a reconstructed polyclinic
register.text: An EIB loan, with an EU grant, to Slovakia’s second-largest city, mainly for energy savings and clean energy in buildings. It modernises primary schools and provides a centre for mothers with children, a senior care facility and a reconstructed polyclinic, serving the education, health and energy standards.

register.name: Operational Programme Slovakia 2021–2027, additional co-financing loan
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 19 June 2026 · additional loan to co-finance key state budget priorities · over 500 infrastructure projects
register.note: To improve access to services for over 1.5 million people
register.text: An additional CEB loan to the Slovak Republic that co-finances national priorities under Operational Programme Slovakia 2021–2027. It supports inclusive education, community-based services, access to employment and support for vulnerable groups, serving the education, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Military and University Hospital East Slovakia, Prešov
register.detail: European Investment Bank · approved 19 November 2025 · total cost about €600M · new premises and the upgrade of the J. A. Reiman hospital in Prešov
register.note: About 932 standard beds, up to 1,236 emergency beds and 17 operating theatres in a dual-use military and civilian university hospital
register.text: Proposed EIB finance for the construction of new premises and the upgrade of the J. A. Reiman hospital in Prešov, a dual-use military and civilian university hospital. It serves the health standard in eastern Slovakia.

register.name: Strategic social investment, Žilina Self-Governing Region
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 9 July 2025 · education, healthcare, social services, transport and sports infrastructure
register.note: Co-finances the region’s strategic projects alongside EU funds
register.text: A CEB loan to the Žilina Self-Governing Region that co-finances strategic projects in education, healthcare, social services, transport and sports infrastructure. It serves the education and health standards.

register.name: Water supply and wastewater, Bratislavská vodárenská spoločnosť
register.detail: European Investment Bank · announced 20 February 2025 · upgrades and extensions of water supply and wastewater infrastructure
register.note: BVS supplies drinking water to approximately 740,000 regular customers
register.text: EIB finance for Bratislava’s municipal water utility to upgrade and extend its water supply and wastewater infrastructure. It increases the reliability of water supply for nearly half a million residents and businesses in Bratislava and serves the water standard.

register.name: Co-financing of EU-supported projects, Programme Slovakia 2021–2027
register.detail: European Investment Bank · €240M signed 20 December 2024, the first part of an €800M loan approved to Slovakia · announced 20 February 2025
register.note: Signed tranches include water and sewerage, education, energy and solid waste
register.text: An EIB loan to the Slovak Republic for the national contributions mandatory for EU-supported projects under Programme Slovakia 2021–2027. It co-finances sustainable water, energy efficiency, renewable energy and education, serving the water, energy and education standards.

register.name: Energy efficiency in the homes of low-income households
register.detail: Modernisation Fund · large-scale scheme · confirmed 7 October 2024 · reference MF 2024-2 SK 0-003 · status active
register.note: Partial renovation of family houses; priority areas include support for low-income households to address energy poverty
register.text: A Modernisation Fund scheme for the partial renovation of the family houses of low-income groups, to cut their energy use and greenhouse gas emissions. It addresses energy poverty, including in rural and remote areas, and serves the energy and shelter standards.

register.name: Power-grid upgrades, ZSE Group
register.detail: European Investment Bank · €350M agreed 5 December 2025 · a further €50M on 3 August 2026 · overhead lines, underground cables, substations, smart meters and grid automation
register.note: ZSE provides electricity distribution services to nearly 2 million customers
register.text: EIB loans to Západoslovenská energetika (ZSE) Group, Slovakia’s largest electricity distribution system operator, to renovate and expand overhead lines and underground cables and deploy smart grid technologies. They let more renewable power, such as solar, enter the system for nearly 2 million customers, serving the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Paloča s.r.o.
items.text: A registered social enterprise of the village of Plaveč that cooks almost 24,000 lunches a year, delivering 110 a day to the homes of retirees in Plaveč and Hromoš, and employs 18 people, 13 of them disadvantaged.
items.source: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family, 2025

items.name: SOCIAL FOOD s.r.o., r.s.p.
items.text: A registered social enterprise in Vyšné Ružbachy that brings groceries twice a week by mobile shop to small villages of the Prešov region, where 121 villages have no food shop, delivering to the homes of people with reduced mobility and filling more than 100 orders a week with six employees with health disadvantages.
items.source: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family, 2025

items.name: Dostupný Domov
items.text: An affordable rental housing company founded by Slovenská sporiteľňa and Slovak Investment Holding that houses 1,111 people in more than 400 flats in 13 cities, where 65% of tenants come from disadvantaged groups and pay rents below market rates.

items.name: Proti prúdu (Nota bene)
items.text: A Bratislava civic association whose street magazine Nota bene, with a monthly print run of 21,000, was sold by 334 vendors across Slovakia in 2024, and which that year supported 36 clients in 25 rental flats through its housing programme.

items.name: ABTEX, s.r.o.
items.text: A Košice maker of work and medical clothing, a protected workshop since 2006 and a registered social enterprise since January 2024, that employs 28 people, 17 of them with health disadvantages.
items.source: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family
